extracted.intended_audience: microbiologists and prokaryote taxonomists preparing new names or requests for Opinions for submission to IJSEM / members of the ICSP
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and recommended minimal standards for forming, describing, and validly publishing names of prokaryotic taxa (including type and neotype procedures) and for preparing Requests for Opinions to the Judicial Commission, as required for publication in IJSEM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Valid publication of the name of a taxon (including a new combination) requires publication in the IJSEM of (a) the name of the taxon, (b) for new taxa the designation of a type, and (c) a description or a reference to an effectively published description of the taxon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fuller details given in following numbered provisions. This is the baseline: name + type (for new taxa) + description/reference must appear in IJSEM for valid publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct form of names (general orthography)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic and suprageneric names are single words in Latin form with an initial capital letter; species names are binary Latin combinations (generic name + specific epithet with initial lowercase); subspecific names are ternary combinations using 'subspecies' (ordinarily 'subsp.') and a subspecific epithet. Names of taxa rank order→tribe have specified suffixes (-ales, -ineae, -aceae, -oideae, -eae, -inae).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not required for validity, the derivation of the name should be given. Where possible include any new names/combinations in the paper title. Follow suffix conventions for ranks from order to subtribe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear explicit indication of new names/combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The name should be clearly proposed as a new name or combination and accepted by the author at time of publication; authors ordinarily append phrases like 'sp. nov.', 'gen. nov.', 'comb. nov.' or make an explicit statement that a new name/combination is being introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revival of names published prior to 1 Jan 1980 but not in Approved Lists may be effected by Rule 33; see additional advice (e.g., report by Chairman of Judicial Commission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of later homonyms
rubrics_metrics.description: The name should not be a later homonym of a previously validly published name of an alga, bacterium, fungus, protozoon, or virus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the IJSB/IJSEM from 1975 onward and Appendices 2 and 3 for published sources of names across groups to check for homonymy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description requirement for valid publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The name must be accompanied by a description of the taxon or by a reference to a previously published description (or reference to an effectively published description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See detailed content requirements below (essential, qualifying, diagnostic characters, strain data, photomicrographs) and conform at least to minimal descriptions approved (Appendix 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a nomenclatural type for new taxa
rubrics_metrics.description: The nomenclatural type of a new taxon should be designated; for species/subspecies that can be cultivated the type strain should be described and designated by the author's strain number and by the accession number(s) under which it is held by at least one culture collection providing access to cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A nomenclatural type is the constituent element to which a taxon name is permanently attached. For species/subspecies that cannot be maintained in culture, the type may be represented by the original description, illustrations, and specimens. Always provide culture collection accession numbers to allow access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neotype strain proposal and establishment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A neotype strain replaces a type strain that can no longer be found. A proposed neotype must be published in IJSEM together with references to the original description/name, a description (or reference) of the proposed neotype, and a record of the author's designation and at least one culture collection accession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The neotype becomes established two years after IJSEM publication (established neotype). Objections must be referred to the Judicial Commission within the first year after publication. A neotype shall be proposed only after a careful search for original strains; if an original strain is later discovered the matter shall be referred immediately to the Judicial Commission. Allowance is made for replacement of an unsuitable type strain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in taxon descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions should include: (a) characteristics essential for membership in the taxon (basic concept); (b) characteristics qualifying the taxon for the next higher taxon; (c) diagnostic characteristics distinguishing the taxon from closely related taxa; and (d) for species, the total number of strains studied, strain designations, and the number of strains positive or negative for each characteristic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If strains are not homogeneous for a characteristic give the specific strain numbers that disagree with the majority so that detailed results can be reconstructed. Include suitable photomicrographs and electron micrographs when appropriate. Descriptions should at least conform to the minimal descriptions approved (see Appendix 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of recommended minimal descriptive standards (Appendix 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist published recommendations for minimal standards of description in IJSEM for many groups (e.g., aerobic endospore-forming bacteria; Bifidobacterium/Lactobacillus; Brucella; Halobacteriales; Halomonadaceae; Helicobacter; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow the group-specific minimal descriptive standards published in IJSEM (list provided and current through July 2014 in Appendix 6). Where subcommittees have drafted standards but not published them, authors should be aware of those drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of a Request for an Opinion (Appendix 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for Exceptions to the rules (Requests for an Opinion) must be accompanied by a fully documented statement of the relevant facts. The title should concisely state the manuscript contents and, if requesting an Opinion, 'Request for an Opinion' should appear as a subtitle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a request lacks adequate evidence it will be returned for revision. An acceptable request will be published in IJSEM and the community invited to submit statements for or against. Challenges to Opinions must state the basis and be supported by documented facts. Submit Requests or challenges to the Editorial Secretary in a form suitable for publication without delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound name formation rules (Appendix 9 A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compound names are formed by combining two or more Latin/Greek word elements into one generic name or specific epithet. Except for the last element only stems are used. The connecting vowel is -o- when the preceding element is Greek, -i- when Latin. A connecting vowel is dropped when the following element starts with a vowel. Hyphens and diacritics are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Thio/bacillus → Thioalkalibacter; connecting vowel exemptions exist for well-established chemical/physical word elements (e.g., thio-, radio-), for oxidation-level vowels (ferro/ferri), and for common prefixes/components (bio-, geo-, halo-, neo-, etc.) where maintaining -o- may aid clarity or follow precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic and subgeneric name rules (Appendix 9 B)
rubrics_metrics.description: A genus (or subgenus) name is a Latin noun in the nominative case. If adjectives or participles are chosen they must be transformed into substantives (nouns) and handled accordingly. The gender of a new genus must be indicated with the etymology given in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjectives associated with genus nouns follow the genus gender. Provide etymology and indicate gender. The appendix lists many common compound endings and their typical grammatical genders (e.g., -bacterium neuter, -coccus masculine, -ia feminine, etc.) and examples of substantivated forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific and subspecific epithet formation and gender agreement (Appendix 9 C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific (or subspecific) epithets must be treated in one of three ways per Rule 12c: (a) as an adjective that agrees in gender with the generic name; (b) as a substantive (noun) in apposition in the nominative case; or (c) as a substantive (noun) in the genitive case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participles are treated as adjectives and fall under Rule 12c. Infinitive (present) participles in the singular have endings -ans, -ens, or -iens depending on the conjugation; perfect participles change with gender. Authors are recommended to check adjectives in a dictionary before use. Table 1 and examples illustrate declensions and endings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominative nouns in apposition and genitive epithets guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominative nouns in apposition must 'make sense' grammatically and functionally to be acceptable as specific epithets (they should meaningfully explain the generic name). Specific epithets ending with -cola or -cida fulfill the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genitive noun formation typically uses dictionary forms; for plural genitives (e.g., 'plantarum') authors must determine declension rules. Provide examples (Desulfovibrio gigas, Escherichia coli) to illustrate nominative vs genitive usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation of prokaryote names from personal names (Appendix 9 D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal names may be used to form generic names or specific epithets, but the Code strongly recommends refraining from naming genera after persons not connected with bacteriology, and recommends that specific epithets derived from personal names recall a person connected with the organism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good practice: ask the person for permission if alive; refrain from naming bacteria after the author or co-authors in the same publication. Two ways to form genus names from personal names are provided (direct endings like -a, -ea, -ia or diminutives -ella, -iella, -nella) and Table 2 gives detailed formation patterns and examples. Not more than one person may be honoured in one name. Rules for handling prefixes/particles (Mac/Mc, O', van, de, Saint/Santo, von, etc.) and rare uses of forenames are provided. In frequent surnames contraction is allowed (e.g., Owenweeksia, Elizabethkingia).
